name: PTSD Coach
one_liner: Free VA app for PTSD symptoms: learn about PTSD, track symptoms, and use coping tools for hard moments. No account needed.
best_for: Veterans and civilians with trauma-related symptoms who want free, private self-help tools
People in trauma therapy who want support between sessions
People not ready for therapy who want to learn about PTSD and start managing symptoms
Anyone who wants a no-account app that keeps entries on the phone
not_for: Anyone in crisis: call or text 988 (veterans press 1)
People looking for a replacement for trauma-focused therapy such as CPT or PE
People who want to talk to a therapist or peer inside the app
short_description: A free VA app with PTSD education, symptom check-ins, tools for coping with distress, and a safety plan.
long_description: PTSD Coach was made by the VA's National Center for PTSD for anyone who has been through trauma, not only veterans. It explains PTSD and its treatment, lets you check your symptoms over time with short questionnaires (including the PC-PTSD-5 screen), and offers tools for managing distress such as grounding, breathing and relaxation exercises, plus a self-guided suicide-prevention safety plan and links to crisis support. It is free with no ads or in-app purchases and needs no account; what you enter stays on your phone. Three randomized trials have tested it: in a 2017 US trial (120 adults) and a 2022 Swedish trial (179 adults) people with access to the app improved more on PTSD and depression symptoms than people on a waitlist, and a 2023 VA trial found that the app with brief clinician support helped primary care veterans more than usual care on self-reported PTSD. It is a self-help tool and does not replace trauma-focused therapy.
patient_summary: PTSD Coach helps you understand PTSD, check how your symptoms are changing, and use quick tools like grounding and breathing when you feel overwhelmed. It is free from the VA, needs no account, and what you enter stays on your phone. You can use it on your own or alongside therapy.

pricing.notes: Free from the VA, with no ads, subscriptions or in-app purchases.

privacy.notes: No account; what you enter stays on your device and VA says it sends no identifying data to VA or third parties. Anonymous usage data is kept for research and can't be deleted because it isn't linked to you; deleting the app removes your entries.

seo.title: PTSD Coach: Free PTSD App from VA | HeyPsych
seo.meta_description: PTSD Coach is a free app for PTSD. Evidence-based grounding tools, symptom tracking, and coping strategies. Developed by the VA.

faqs.q: Is PTSD Coach only for veterans?
faqs.a: No. While developed by the VA, PTSD Coach is designed for anyone with PTSD symptoms, whether from combat, assault, accidents, or other traumatic events. The app is free for everyone.

faqs.q: Can PTSD Coach replace trauma therapy?
faqs.a: PTSD Coach is a self-help tool, not a replacement for trauma-focused therapy like CPT or PE. For moderate to severe PTSD, evidence-based therapy is recommended. PTSD Coach works well as a supplement to therapy or first step toward treatment.

faqs.q: What can I do in PTSD Coach?
faqs.a: PTSD Coach includes: self-assessment (PCL-5), symptom tracking, psychoeducation about PTSD, grounding exercises, breathing techniques, cognitive coping tools, safety planning, and professional support resources.

faqs.q: Is PTSD Coach safe if I'm triggered?
faqs.a: PTSD Coach includes grounding exercises designed to help when you're triggered. However, if you're in crisis, please contact the Veterans Crisis Line (988, press 1), 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline, or your local emergency services.
